title: Comin' Thro' the Rye
description: The Scottish song, for 2 to 4 singers: two verses of "Gin a body meet a body", as printed in Edinburgh in 1848. The soprano sings the melody with its Scotch snaps, the alto sings the words mostly in thirds and sixths beneath it, the tenor fills in the chord, and the bass sings the low line.

licence.words: public domain: traditional, reworked from the song Robert Burns (died 1796) wrote for the Scots Musical Museum, vol. 5 (James Johnson, died 1811; Edinburgh, 1796), no. 417; an earlier form of these words is no. 418 there; these words as printed in 1848 by G. F. Graham (died 1867)
licence.tune: public domain: traditional; this form printed in the Scots Musical Museum, vol. 5 (James Johnson, died 1811; Edinburgh, 1796), no. 418, "Comin thro' the rye. 2d Sett", and in 1848 arranged by T. M. Mudie (died 1876)
licence.source: melody and words from G. F. Graham (editor), The Songs of Scotland, adapted to their appropriate melodies, vol. II (Wood and Co., Edinburgh, 1848), pp. 10 to 11, "Comin' thro' the rye", arranged by T. M. Mudie (Thomas Molleson Mudie, 1809 to 1876) for voice and piano, marked Moderato, crotchet = 72; printed in G in 4/4 and written here in G; read from the scan at archive.org/details/songsofscotlanda00grah (University of Toronto, the three volumes bound in one), leaves 196 and 197 (https://archive.org/details/songsofscotlanda00grah/page/n196), checked against the National Library of Scotland copy, archive.org/details/songsofscotland01grah, leaves 18 and 19; the same tune, in B-flat with an earlier form of these words ("Ilka body has a body" for "Ilka lassie has her laddie"), is no. 418 in the Scots Musical Museum, vol. 5 (Johnson, Edinburgh, 1796), p. 431, archive.org/details/scotsmusicalmuv300john, leaf 28. Verse 1 is the verse printed under the notes; verse 2 is Graham's first printed stanza after it ("Comin' frae the well"); his third stanza ("Comin' frae the town") and Miss Stephens's closing lines are left out to keep the song near a minute. Every pitch and rhythm as printed, with two printed grace notes left out (F#4 before "bo-" of "Need a body", B4 before "has"); Graham's slurred pairs on "ha'e", "smile" and "at" sung by the tune on one syllable and by the other parts on one note. Breath written in for beginners: "I!" (and "I;" in verse 2), printed as a dotted crotchet, sung as a crotchet so all parts breathe before "Yet" and "But"; the other lines start after the printed crotchet rests. Tempo 60, slower than Graham's 72 (the Museum marks its set "Very Slow"), so no syllable is shorter than a quarter of a second. The fermata on "me" and the ritenuto before it are left to the singers. Mudie's piano part used only to check the chords; the voice parts are Stackapella's own. Words as printed, "Gin" footnoted "If" and "Ilka" "Each; every"; Graham notes "kiss" is often sung "greet".
